title: Roofing Software: 7 Tools for Measuring, Proposals and Jobs
html:
Roofing software pays off when it matches how a roof job actually moves: measure, propose, schedule the crew and collect. Most roofers need a measurement tool, a proposal and job board, and a free Google Business Profile before anything else. Pair them with roofing SEO so estimate requests keep arriving. Published prices in this guide run from $0 to $750 a month, and one vendor publishes none.

Roofing software has to answer one question for the office: what is the status of every roof right now? A roofing company runs several jobs at once, each with a measurement, a proposal, a material order and a crew date. Tools help when they hold that chain in one place. This guide covers seven tools, the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Roofing is a high-ticket, low-frequency sale. One lead can be worth thousands of dollars, so a slow follow-up costs more than a cheap app saves. The tools below are grouped by the step they speed up. Several of them charge per measurement or per project rather than per month, so the math differs from other trades.

Which roofing software measures roofs and builds proposals?

Roofr and Hover both turn a roof into measurements, and they charge in different ways. Roofr sells monthly plans with pay-per-report measurements, and Hover charges per project with optional yearly plans.

  • Roofr: the Starter plan is $0 with unlimited users and measurement reports at $19 each. Essentials is $249 a month billed monthly and adds unlimited proposals, invoices, e-signatures and card or ACH payments. Scale is $349 a month billed monthly and adds crew management and QuickBooks integration. Limit: Starter allows only 10 trial proposals, invoices and work orders, and the yearly prices on the page are unclear, so confirm them with Roofr.
  • Hover: Starter has no subscription and the first 3 projects are free. A roof-only scan costs $29 for a simple roof, $49 for an average roof and $69 for a complex roof on Starter. Pro is $999 a year and takes $20 off each project. Limit: Pro covers a single branch, and credits expire after 12 months or if you cancel.

The two models suit different volumes. On Roofr, a roofer who measures 20 roofs a month pays about $380 on Starter at $19 each. Essentials costs $249 plus $13 a report, which is about $509 for the same 20. Starter stays cheaper until roughly 42 reports a month, but it caps proposals.

On Hover, the $999 Pro plan saves $20 on every project. That means the plan pays for itself at about 50 projects a year, or four a month.

What roofing contractor software runs the whole job pipeline?

AccuLynx and Leap are the platforms roofers compare when they want leads, jobs and documents in one system. They price very differently.

  • AccuLynx: the pricing page shows a Get Pricing request and a Talk to Sales button instead of plan prices. Limit: you cannot compare cost until you speak with a rep, so plan time for a demo.
  • Leap: lists Essential at $79 a month for 1 user. Team starts at $298 a month with the first user included, and Premium starts at $750 with 6 users. Extra Team users are $99 each. Limit: all plans are one-year contracts paid monthly, and Essential allows only 5 digital signatures.

Leap's published prices let you do the math. A Team plan with six users costs $298 plus five extra seats at $99, which is $793 a month. Premium lists six users at $750. At that size Premium costs less than Team, so check which tier fits your headcount before you sign.

Ask AccuLynx and Leap the same questions. Who owns the customer data if you leave? What does onboarding cost? How do material orders and supplier pricing connect? A pipeline tool is only as good as the data your office enters into it.

Which general field service apps work for a small roofing crew?

Jobber and Housecall Pro are general field service apps, not roofing-specific tools. A small crew that quotes, schedules and invoices can use them for the basics.

  • Jobber: Core for 1 user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Extra users on higher plans cost $29 a month each. Limit: card processing is 2.9% plus 30 cents, and add-ons such as Marketing Suite at $99 a month are billed on top.
  • Housecall Pro: Basic is $59 a month billed annually for 1 user, and Essentials is $149 a month annual for 5 users. Max is $299 annual for 8 users. Limit: Basic has one user, and several add-ons have no price on the page.

Neither page lists aerial measurements, so a roofer using these still needs a measurement tool from the first group. That combination can cost less than a full roofing platform. It also means two logins and a manual step between the measurement and the quote.

What free tool puts a roofing company on the map?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows a roofing company in Google Maps when a homeowner searches for roof repair nearby. Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, phone number, photos and reviews. Limit: it needs accurate address details and steady photos, posts and review replies to stand out.

Photos of finished roofs and quick replies to reviews carry most of the weight.

RoofrMeasurements, proposals, job board$0 Starter, $249 and $349 monthly plansStarter caps trial documents
HoverProperty measurements$0 plan, $999 a year ProCredits expire in 12 months
AccuLynxRoofing job platformNot publishedNeeds a sales call
LeapSales and job platform$79 to $750 a monthOne-year contracts
JobberGeneral field service$29 to $49 a month for CoreNo aerial measurements listed
Housecall ProGeneral field service$59 to $299 a month, billed annuallyAdd-ons not priced
Google Business ProfileMap listingFreeNeeds steady upkeep

What does roofing software not do for a roofer?

Roofing software organizes jobs after the lead arrives. It does not rank your website, run ads or answer the phone, and none of the tools above does those things for you.

Your website is the front door. A quote form that feeds your job tool saves retyping. It is a managed build, not a template you edit yourself.

How much does roofing software cost for a three-crew company?

A three-crew roofing company measuring 30 roofs a month has several ways to buy. On Roofr Essentials, the plan is $249 a month and 30 reports at $13 add $390, so the bill is about $639. On Starter, 30 reports at $19 cost $570, but proposals are capped at 10 trial documents.

On Hover, 30 average roof-only scans cost $1,470 a month on Starter at $49 each. On Pro they cost $870 at $29 each, plus the $999 yearly fee, which is about $83 a month.

Measurement volume drives the bill more than the plan fee. A company that measures every lead pays for many reports that never become jobs. A company that measures only after a signed inspection pays for fewer. Decide when in the sales process a measurement is worth its cost, and write that rule down for the sales team.

Add the job board on top. Leap Team with four users costs $298 plus three seats at $99, which is $595 a month. Housecall Pro Essentials covers five users for $149 a month billed annually. The cheapest plan is not always the right one, because a tool the crew will not use wastes every dollar.

What should you ask a roofing software vendor before you sign?

Ask five questions in the demo and write down the answers. Vendors change plans often, so a written answer beats the page you read today.

Run that storm-week test during any free trial. Hover gives the first 3 projects free, and Jobber lists a 14-day trial of its Grow plan. If entering a lead takes more than a few minutes, the office will skip it when the phones are busy.

How do you choose roofing software for your company?

Choose roofing software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it measure, propose and schedule, or only one of the three, and does it handle your insurance and retail jobs?

Cost: add the plan price, extra users, per-report fees and card processing, then compare the total with one average roof.

Setup effort: can the office build proposal templates and import customers in a week, or does it need paid onboarding?

A one-crew roofer can run on Roofr Starter, Jobber Core and a free Google Business Profile. The listed cost is $19 per measurement plus $29 to $49 a month. A roofer with two or three crews fits Roofr Essentials or Scale, or Housecall Pro Essentials with a separate measurement tool.

A larger company with sales reps, several offices and material orders should book demos with AccuLynx and Leap and compare written quotes. Whatever you choose, give the office one rule: every lead and every roof gets entered the same day.

Set a short rollout plan before you buy anything. Week one, enter every open lead and active job. Week two, build one proposal template for repairs and one for replacements. Week three, move crew scheduling onto the board. Cancel inside the trial or first month if the office is not using it by then.

Software works hardest when leads keep coming. For a related trade, read the handyman software guide.

What software does a roofing company need?

A roofing company needs a way to measure roofs, send proposals, schedule crews and collect payment. It also needs a Google Business Profile and a website so homeowners can find it. Start with measurements and proposals, then add a full job board once several crews run at once.

Published prices here run from $0 for Roofr Starter to $750 a month for Leap Premium. Hover and Roofr also charge per measurement. AccuLynx publishes no price. Processing fees, extra users and add-ons cost more, so confirm the total for your crew size with each vendor.

Is Roofr or Hover better for measuring roofs?

Roofr charges $19 per report on Starter and $13 on paid plans. Hover charges $29 to $69 per roof-only scan on Starter. Roofr bundles proposals and a job board, while Hover is mainly a measurement tool. Compare the cost per roof at your monthly volume.

Does AccuLynx publish its prices?

No. The AccuLynx shows a Get Pricing request and a Talk to Sales button instead of plan prices. Ask for a written quote that lists every user, add-on and onboarding fee. Then compare it with the published prices of Leap and Roofr.

Can a roofer use Jobber or Housecall Pro?

Yes, for scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments. Neither lists aerial measurements, so a roofer still needs a measurement tool. Jobber lists Core at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists Basic at $59 a month billed annually.

Is Google Business Profile free for a roofing company?

Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: accurate service areas, photos of finished roofs and replies to every review. Google's paid ad products, such as Local Service Ads, are separate and carry their own costs.

What should a new roofing company buy first?

Set up a free Google Business Profile and a simple website first, because estimate requests come before jobs. Then add a measurement tool and a proposal template. Add a full job board once you run more than one crew at a time.

does it measure, propose and schedule, or only one of the three, and does it handle your insurance and retail jobs?
Cost:
add the plan price, extra users, per-report fees and card processing, then compare the total with one average roof.
Setup effort:
can the office build proposal templates and import customers in a week, or does it need paid onboarding?
A one-crew roofer can run on Roofr Starter, Jobber Core and a free Google Business Profile. The listed cost is $19 per measurement plus $29 to $49 a month. A roofer with two or three crews fits Roofr Essentials or Scale, or Housecall Pro Essentials with a separate measurement tool.
A larger company with sales reps, several offices and material orders should book demos with AccuLynx and Leap and compare written quotes. Whatever you choose, give the office one rule: every lead and every roof gets entered the same day.
Set a short rollout plan before you buy anything. Week one, enter every open lead and active job. Week two, build one proposal template for repairs and one for replacements. Week three, move crew scheduling onto the board. Cancel inside the trial or first month if the office is not using it by then.
Software works hardest when leads keep coming. For a related trade, read the handyman software guide.
###
What software does a roofing company need?
A roofing company needs a way to measure roofs, send proposals, schedule crews and collect payment. It also needs a Google Business Profile and a website so homeowners can find it. Start with measurements and proposals, then add a full job board once several crews run at once.
###
How much does roofing software cost?
Published prices here run from $0 for Roofr Starter to $750 a month for Leap Premium. Hover and Roofr also charge per measurement. AccuLynx publishes no price. Processing fees, extra users and add-ons cost more, so confirm the total for your crew size with each vendor.
###
Is Roofr or Hover better for measuring roofs?
Roofr charges $19 per report on Starter and $13 on paid plans. Hover charges $29 to $69 per roof-only scan on Starter. Roofr bundles proposals and a job board, while Hover is mainly a measurement tool. Compare the cost per roof at your monthly volume.
###
Does AccuLynx publish its prices?
No. The AccuLynx shows a Get Pricing request and a Talk to Sales button instead of plan prices. Ask for a written quote that lists every user, add-on and onboarding fee. Then compare it with the published prices of Leap and Roofr.
###
Can a roofer use Jobber or Housecall Pro?
Yes, for scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments. Neither lists aerial measurements, so a roofer still needs a measurement tool. Jobber lists Core at $49 a month with no commitment. Housecall Pro lists Basic at $59 a month billed annually.
###
Is Google Business Profile free for a roofing company?
Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: accurate service areas, photos of finished roofs and replies to every review. Google's paid ad products, such as Local Service Ads, are separate and carry their own costs.
###
What should a new roofing company buy first?
Set up a free Google Business Profile and a simple website first, because estimate requests come before jobs. Then add a measurement tool and a proposal template. Add a full job board once you run more than one crew at a time.
